# 1 Enoch Chapter 78 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**78:1** And-the-names of-the-sun are-the-following: the-first Orjares, and-the-second Tomas.

**78:2** And-the-moon has-four-names: the-first-name is-Asonja, the-second Ebla, the-third Benase, and-the-fourth Erae.

**78:3** These-are-the-two great-luminaries: their-circumference is-like-the-circumference of-the-heaven, and-the-size of-the-circumference of-both-is-alike.

**78:4** In-the-circumference of-the-sun there-are-seven-portions-of-light which-are-added-to-it more-than-to-the-moon, and-in-definite-measures it-is-transferred till-the-seventh-portion-of-the-sun is-exhausted.

**78:5** And-they-set and-enter-the-portals of-the-west, and-make-their-revolution by-the-north, and-come-forth through-the-eastern-portals on-the-face-of-the-heaven.

**78:6** And-when the-moon-rises, one-half of-her is-towards-the-sun, and-on-that-night in-the-beginning of-her-morning she-waxes, and-she-turns-away from-the-sun; and-she-is-illuminated as-she-recedes-from-the-sun, but-her-illumination grows-and-reaches-its-fullness.

**78:7** And-after she-is-separated-from-the-sun she-completes-the-remainder of-her-journey for-the-rest of-the-month, in-eighteen-parts of-her-light she-diminishes through-all-the-night till-on-the-first-day her-light-is-destroyed; and-she-completes-the-month in-eighteen-portions and-three-tens and-one-part.

**78:8** Her-year-has-three-hundred-and-fifty-four-days; and-the-sum-of-the-days-of-the-moon is-three-hundred-and-fifty-four-days.

**78:9** And-the-longer-period amounts-to thirty-days belonging-to-one-of-the-five-intercalary-days, in-that-it-comes-every-fifth-year.

**78:10** [There-are-thirty-days-in-this-period.] Therefore-there-are-five-years-of-the-sun in-three-hundred-and-sixty-five-days each, and-the-total of-these-five-years-is-one-thousand-and-eight-hundred-and-twenty-five-days.

**78:11** And-the-total-of-the-days-of-the-moon in-five-years-amounts-to-one-thousand-seven-hundred-and-seventy-days; and-the-difference between-these-two-is-fifty-five-days, and-there-are-eleven-days-missing-from-the-moon-per-year.

**78:12** And-the-year-is-accurately-completed-in-correspondence-with-their-world-stations-and-in-correspondence-with-the-stations-of-the-sun which-rise-from-the-portals-through-which-they-rise-and-set-for-thirty-days.

**78:13** Uriel-showed-me-another-ordering and-I-saw-the-divisions-of-all-the-stars-of-heaven.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) text. The names of the sun (Orjares, Tomas) and moon (Asonja, Ebla, Benase, Erae) in v. 1-2 are enigmatic names found only in the Ethiopic tradition; their etymology is uncertain. V. 8 gives the lunar year as 354 days, confirming the 10-day annual deficit from the 364-day solar year.*
